Comment: I was brought in by a friend after taking some newly prescribed medication and having a bad reaction to it. I was slurring my speech, unable to walk or see clearly, had difficulty breathing and chest pains. She had looked up the medication online and was concerned that the combination I was on could be leading to the reaction, and was specifically worried about serotonin syndrome, so she called Telehealth who told us to immediately go to the ER. When we arrived at the ER all of this was relayed to the hospital staff; my friend stayed with me as I was unable to speak. When we moved into the waiting room my friend was left to sit on the floor as there were no seats. She sat there for about an hour while I was propped up in a chair. When we were finally led to an examination room to see a doctor, she started to tell him all of my symptoms and her concerns. He laughed and said this was all normal when taking anti-depressants. My friend was surprised by this and said she was specifically concerned about serotonin syndrome and he brushed that off. She asked what symptoms we should be concerned about, as the information she found online, what she was told by Telehealth, and her own experience had led her to believe this was serious, and he told her 'if you're going to immediately kill yourself, come in'. She confirmed that he was saying there were no symptoms to watch out for, and that unless I was suicidal, there was no reason to visit - he confirmed. As he was leaving (this all lasted about 2 minutes) he told her that I should stop taking Sertroline immediately since it was what was causing the trouble - she pointed out I had been on that for years, and it was more likely the addition of Buspirone from a day ago that was causing this issue: he disregarded this. He then said that I couldn't go off of Sertroline quickly because of withdrawal, and left. At no point were any vitals taken, no one asked about medical history, the doctor literally laughed at my symptoms and left us with the impression that somehow, all was fine. I was referred to emergency by my physician as at the time they were referring everyone to emergency as a precautionary measure to rule out COVID as some of my symptoms fit the criteria. While my COVID results were thankfully negative, I noted that the test had NOT been cleared or approved by XXXXXXXXXXXXX. This is important information that should have been relayed to patient prior to taking the test. Having said that, the intake process and triage services could be improved significantly, as it can set the tone for the remainder of the processes and procedures during emergency visits. It can also help to relieve anxiety in patients who are already under stress/pain. Below are a few issues that I encountered, and hope they can help to improve services moving forward: 1. Triage should take time to listen to the patient's symptoms and ensure that the correct complaint is recorded for the doctor to review: I went in for possible food poisoning / possible parasitic infection, however the intake nurse wrote down 'sore throat:' so I had to re-explain my situation to the doctor in order to receive the correct tests. 2. There was a nurse(?) or volunteer (?) who was taking everyone's vitals prior to seeing triage. While I did observe the nurse wiping equipment down between each patient, it seemed that it was done in a very automatic and disengaged manner. I was concerned and extra vigilant because the gentleman before me (in a tank top and shorts) was covered in open wounds and sores on his entire body that were oozing blood and pus. The nurse carelessly and quickly wiped down the blood pressure cuff *** but only the velcro part ***but not the area that had direct contact to the gentleman's skin and subsequently, mine. I politely asked her to disinfect the cuff, and she stated that she already had (she was not rude, however as a health professional I would expect a little more care and concern). I did not pursue this because there is a fear that they will tell security, who will always side with the professionals. I immediately washed my arms and covered them with large amounts of sanitizer/disinfectant to prevent any transfer of bacteria/viruses from his bodily fluids. For the 8+ hours I was in emergency, I had anxiety about contracting MRSA's or other diseases because of this. This leads me to my next suggestion. Emergency departments should have a separate clinic for fractures and other straight forward issues that don't require in-depth diagnostics etc. to expedite treatment and limit exposure to other illnesses. There have been numerous cases of otherwise healthy individuals contracting infections from emergency and hospital visits during their lengthy wait, as they are exposed to all manner of illnesses. Thank you to all staff for your service during these extraordinary times.

Lengthy waiting period between each test that was taken

Let me start off by saying that I am type 2 diabetic. My surgery was to have taken place at 8:45AM and we were to be at the hospital at 6:45 AM (I haven't had anything to eat or drink for 12 hrs.) ... we were there at 6:30 AM. My time for surgery came and went. A doctor did come to me around 9:30 AM and said that they were sorry that a piece of equipment needed for my surgery hadn't arrived, so my surgery was going to be at 10 AM My surgery did not take place until 1:10 PM as there was some sort of mix-up in scheduling or some lame excuse ... which was unacceptable. We waited in the waiting area for 6 hrs. Someone was not on the ball here! My stay in the hospital was extended from overnight as a result to 2 days. I have to say the food was excellent and the day nurses were great! The night nurses were also nice, but extremely loud in the hallway and it made it impossible to sleep. I did complain to the night nurse, I believe that she was a trainee? All in all, though, the hospital stay was great, All of the Doctors & Nurses were great. It was just the whole admitting problem that occurred that was the problem!!
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Admit/Registration, Dietary/Service, Doctor/Physician, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient

Comment: Level of education is low because the visit was for my X-year-old son The doctor was very polite and kind. He was also very thorough - ordered extra scans to make sure my son did not have head trauma (fell off his bed)
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Information/Education, Respect to Patient

Comment: Limit people accompanying patients - advising people if their problem/issue could have been better served @ walk in clinic as there are plenty of clinic Educating people of cost & role of emergency department Revamp waiting areas

Comment: Long gaps in service if you don't know what the time line is going to be The staff is very busy and have a hard time stopping and giving information

Long waiting. Spent 6 hours on my visit. With pain they didn't give me medicine for pain. They just did the laboratory and wait for result and gave medicine to stop my bleeding but no medication for pain.

Comment: Long waits Not enough space to wait comfortably Dirty Not enough staff - renovations make hospital confusing to get around. Symptoms were brushed off by ER doctor! Comment: Lots of police presence Being able to bring children into their own waiting room is important.
Lousy Food
Loved the aquarium Put my son "the patient" at ease after a serious head injury.
Loved the nurses and doctors. I was well taken care of. Thank you.
Lovely birthing experience, thank you to all staff. Would love to see a birthing tub added and open up access to alternative pain management during pandemic (ie gas).
Lovely people cheerful Easy to approach
Lung pain heart pain only sometime test blood
Magnificent team! My nurse XXXXX - many thanks! I am happy about my non medicated labor!

Mainly a missed diagnosis was my concern. I had an xray and the emerg dr missed pneumonia. Not sure if it was hard to see or not. But I did remember that I didn't feel like he listened to my chest like my regular dr does. I went to my regular gp two days later and he said it sounded like pneumonia and put me on antibiotics right away without the xray. 3 days later the hospital contacted me because the radiologist saw pneumonia where the emerg dr didn't. It was nice that they followed up and checked. That was good to know. Again I don't know if it was hard to see or if the emerg dr was delinquent but it did seem to me that he was not as focused as he might have been (combination of not really doing a full listen and missing it on the xray makes me think that) anyway I am on the mend. Would have been nice to have had it for a few days less and start healing a few days sooner. Not sure if there is anything systematic that could have been done to increases my chances of having been diagnosed more accurately at the time. Have a sneaking suspicion that a more thorough checklist for listening to chest protocol would have increased likelihood of an accurate diagnoses at the time. All the best.

Majority of delivery experience was excellent - specially due to individual people (nurse XXXXX and Dr. XXXXXX) Some concerns we experienced were: after admission by resident, we were only assessed by full physician after 5 hours. THere was poor communication to us, we were told multiple times doctor would assess us 'soon.' Despite informing nurse wish to not receive antibiotics for GBs+ until after membranes ruptured, she encouraged Mom that doctor was coming soon and would want to rupture membranes (not wish of Mom) and therefore encouraged to start antibiotics right away. Therefore 3 unneeded doses of antibiotics doses were received before waters were eventually broken at 9 am. Nurses placed 2 IVs in wrist. Despite being told they were painful, nurses reluctant to replace them. Pain in iv sites lasted weeks after birth. Since opted for private room, we stayed in delivery room for rest of our stay. This was far from nurses and we didn't see a nurse from initial shift change until 2 am when we had to call the nurse to receive a bassinet. Also, the room was not cleaned after the delivery. The placenta was left in a bag at the door. The garbage smelled of blood and my mother had to empty the garbages and linens. I passed a very large blood clot on the day after delivery. We had to ask the nurse to assess my vitals initially and after several hours. They were reluctant saying that the policy for routine vitals wasn't due yet, despite a large amount of blood passing and us being concerned. A large amount of education was presented in a rush right before discharge, this was overwhelming. During the rest of our stay after baby came , we rarely saw a nurse. This could have been spread out during stay to allow time to process and ask questions.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Housekeeping/Room, Information/Education, Medication/Prescrip, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Positive Recognition

Comment: Many sick people wait hours to see a doctor. We really need to improve the waiting time wait. Also, hire more doctors. Some seem under stressed and too many patients, yet not enough doctors. XXXXX.

Maybe just me but I did not know what to do afterwards, one document can not cover everything. First time in the hospital it was not always clear. Miscommunication after. I can't go to ED more than 3 times and that is what it feels. I had questions and did not know where to go with those questions. Everything is time in the health system. Understand they are busy but you don't get proper time. I did not have questions at the time but later I did. I called the health line but it usually ends contact your doctor. Overall it was really good. Nurses were excellent.
Code: Continuity/Transition, Emergency Dept, Information/Education, Nurse/Nurse aide

Comment: Meals provided were not healthy which is ironic considering it's a hospital.

Meals were completely unpalatable because I was put on a no sodium diet. Although I have type 2 diabetes, my blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol; are all well controlled with metformin, indapamide and rosuvastatin - my physicians have never put me on a sodium restricted diet. During my stay all of the meals, without exception, were so bland and tasteless that they went back uneaten except for fresh fruit which was served only rarely and coffee which was served only once daily. Everything about my stay was excellent except for the food.

Meals--Although I have been told hospital food is never very good, I personally thought the meals were quite good. Volume of food given at each meal--remembering, I am XX years old, I thought that there was far too much food received at each meal. Again, perhaps many patients have no trouble eating everything that is dished up to them but I thought, if in fact you do check on how much is not eaten or thrown out, perhaps the hospital could save $ by cutting back to some extent. I was also very pleased with the doctors and radiology staff who cared for me.
Meatloaf with mushroom gravy was dried out and not at all appetizing.

Medical residents who attend to patients, particularly young children, should be more cautious of their approach and assessments. The medical resident was not even near friendly with my son and proceeded to describe the medical situation as potential mumps, an infection, or CANCER. These residents should be trained to have better 'bed-side manners' and not send parents into a frenzy with that type of assessment. It was the most unprofessional and disturbing assessment received by a resident - with no tact.
Code: Doctor/Physician, Emotional Support, Respect to Patient

Comment: Midwife team was exceptional and nurses were helpful with IV. Other than the anesthesiologist we didn't see any other hospital staff during the duration of our stay.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Nurse/Nurse aide, Respect to Patient

Comment: Miscommunication about my vegetarian diet. Was served ham at mealtime. Was corrected by next meal.
Misdiagnosed by paediatrician. Would not recommend to other parents of newborns.
More comfy seating and water dispensers.
More coordination between ambulatory care & emergency care needed. Otherwise OK.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Emergency Dept, Parking/Transport

Comment: More info about why and how long you may be waiting

More info re what my condition is when possible - ie is this something where I will have to be admitted to hospital or will I likely be allowed to return home with care instructions and or medications.

More information for women about vaginal healing/pelvic health after labour/delivery. I was lucky to have a midwife team to check in on my post-delivery healing but I know many women are told to go to the emergency room if they have problems. Women should also be advised on pelvic floor therapy as a great way to assess/heal any potential complications from pregnancy/birth.
More information on how to deal with being a new diabetic would have been helpful.

Most of my answers have been affected by the tiny semi private room we were stuck in. It was a very busy night and they had nothing else available but being that my husband and I are quite tall lanky people we were quite uncomfortable maneuvering around the tiny draped off section we were given. My answers were also affected by the fact that I was a very calm person. I had no sense of panic and just went with the flow so I was lacking a sense of urgency. Our daytime nurse was PHENOMENAL Went above and beyond to help us.

Most of the negative points were the result of one nurse in particular who did not seem to know what was going on with my treatment and discharge, and though I think she was trying to help, she caused more trouble than good (ie told me I could go fill prescription at the pharmacy before discharge - approx 34 hrs after my c-section, which was a difficult walk for me and took 25 min, to find that it was closed, of course, at 6:30 pm, though I had asked specifically if it was open still so late). She gave me some other misinformation as well, then corrected it later on. Also, I was not aware that I had ever been visited by a doctor during my stay aside from my family doctor who came by - I learned before I left that one of the young women I had thought was a nurse, was in fact a doctor (I have bad hearing so I missed that, but it could have been clearer?)
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Discharge, Doctor/Physician, Information/Education, Medication/Prescrip, Nurse/Nurse aide

Comment: Most of the time I have been treated at the emergency department I have received good care the worst experience was when the doctor said I "almost" had a heart attack. You either have one or you don't. There is no between. Several times I have been refused pain medication
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Emergency Dept, Medication/Prescrip

Comment: Most of the times when I asked to speak to the doctor, the nurses would tell me that they've called him to come to me but he never showed up. My daughters tried to speak to the doctor because we had to leave because our night that was scheduled for that afternoon, and he rudely turned them away.
Code: Doctor/Physician, Nurse/Nurse aide, Respect to Patient

Comment: Most of this survey wasn't applicable to me. I gave birth with a midwife and didn't deal with any doctors, and only dealt with a couple nurses after the birth. My newborn was taken to NICU immediately, so I didn't receive any info on how to care for my baby upon discharge. I was disappointed that we were not able to upgrade to a private room and that we were told they were being 'saved' in case they were needed for COVID? We had just dealt with a traumatic birth and our baby was in the NICU, we would have loved some privacy and quiet - especially when willing to pay extra. We would understand if there weren't any available, but we weren't really given a good excuse as to why we couldn't get one. There was a disconnect between the NICU and the nurses. A NICU staff member told us we would be able to stay in the hospital for additional nights since our baby was in NICU and we had yet to have heard any news about our discharge from any nurses. We weren't told about our discharge until an hour prior. As you can imagine, this was devastating to us at the time since we weren't expecting to leave our baby at the hospital, especially so abruptly. Our baby was not premature so we were not expecting a long stay. Upon our discharge, the nurse was making light of the fact that our baby was not leaving with us. She made comments like 'I keep thinking I'm forgetting something, but it's just because your baby's not going home with you' and 'I guess we don't have to do the car seat test, haha'. This left a horrendous taste in our mouths and made the fact that we were going home without our newborn baby, with an empty car seat, and not knowing when she would be coming home much more difficult. Some empathy or at least some decent bedside manner would have been appreciated. The nurses station was also quite loud overnight and I had a very hard time sleeping with the noise. Also, in the gender section of this survey, Trans is misspelled as Tran.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Discharge, ICU/CCU, Information/Education, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient

Comment: Mr. XXXXXXXX and the nursing staff were excellent. My only suggestion would be to have a cleaner shower area in the recovery room as it looked as though the walls had not been cleaned.
Ms. XXXXXXXXXXX, Ms. XXXXXXXXXXXXXX and Ms. XXXXXXXXXXXXX, nurses from XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, were especially helpful and empathetic.
Code: Emotional Support, Nurse/Nurse aide, Respect to Patient, Positive Recognition

Comment: Much better experience with this stay compared to my first stay. However, it may be because the nurses this time around knew I myself am a XXXXX. The first time I stayed at the hospital after delivery of my first born, the staff didn't know I am a XXXXX and the treatment was quite different.

My admission was very slow. My info package said to go to one location but I was asked to go back to the pre admissions area next door. A new staff person was being trained and the process was so slow that medical staff involved in eye surgeries were furious as their surgeries were being held up. They even began administering drops to waiting room patients. The staff, including the volunteer were all very pleasant and but I was very concerned as the time of my surgery approached and I was still waiting to be processed. I was also surprised that much of the pre admissions info had to be repeated. I would have thought that this info would be carried forward automatically to admissions forms which would have spread up the process for me and everyone else.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Admit/Registration, Respect to Patient

Comment: My ambulance drivers were wonderful! Very accommodating people I give them high marks. Overall my experience was satisfactory regarding my care

My appointment with my health care team was constantly interrupted by various people entering the room and demanding the doctor's attention. My health concerns were not addressed as the doctor was distracted and had to leave the room on several occasions. I was dismissed before all my questions were answered, and I was told I would have to wait 6 months for another appointment. I was treated unprofessionally and disrespectfully.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Emotional Support, Information/Education, Respect to Patient

Comment: My appreciation to all health care providers in the emergency dept. Thank you!

My attending Doctor was cognitive of my discomfort, bot physically and emotionally, and took excellent of my needs, concerns, and worries. He was pleasant to be around during my stay. He deserves commendation for his mindfulness towards me.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Emotional Support, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient

Comment: My baby was born with a cleft palate, so I was not able to breastfeed. We paid to rent a hospital breast pump, but there wasn't one available, so I wasn't able to express milk to feed the baby. This was not a good experience.

My baby was placed in the NICU as a result of birth trauma during my stay at XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. The maternity ward was extremely poorly equipped for supporting a mother with a baby in the NICU. Specifically, travelling between the locked doors of the maternity ward and the NICU (especially after a c-section under general anaesthetic) was very difficult, I was not treated with respect by the nurses in the maternity ward, I was rushed out of my hospital room and questioned for my medical decisions, I was harassed about breast feeding when my milk had not come in. Policies and procedures should be put in place for mothers with babies in the NICU - it is not acceptable to treat them in the same way as mothers who have their babies in their rooms - the circumstances are very different. As well, travelling between the NICU and maternity ward should be made easier - significant stress was put upon my husband and I as we needed to travel to the NICU several times a day and the layout of the hospital did not make this easy. In addition, I was extremely disappointed and offended by some of the nursing care in the ward. I would be happy to provide more details if you would like to contact me directly.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Emotional Support, ICU/CCU, Information/Education, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient

Comment: My basic observation is understaffed, needs upgrading in terms of ac, among other things, need a new building. In the ER, there was a PSW was present in case of aggression when my husband was never aggressive. ER is severely understaffed. Hoping for some quick improvements in this regard. Told of 8 hour backlog.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Emergency Dept, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort

Comment: My bed was never changed in 4 days. I was never offered a towel to get washed up. The food was terrible.

My bedding and nightgown were never change during a 4 day stay. The floor was ever washed. I used a commode, but no one came to help me when I rang and no one came to empty it, so I might use it more than once before it was emptied. No one even straightened my bed or asked me if I wanted to get washed or brush teeth. I had to get out of bed on my own even though I just had a knee replacement. I have to say I was very impressed by the pre-op set up. It all went downhill once I was admitted. Also the food is absolutely horrendous and inedible.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Dietary/Service, Housekeeping/Room, Physical Comfort, Infection Prevention & Control

Comment: My biggest difficulty was trying to sleep. Room and corridor was very loud. The announcements were loud and came throughout the night

My biggest trouble was getting someone to assist with my physical problems. My legs swelled up. I was not supposed to not do anything. but the nurses would not help me. They looked at me poorly. I had to go to the bathroom. I was using a commode. I could not get there fast enough and I wet myself. The nurse put me to bed without offering to help me clean myself. Some nurses were good. Others were not. One nurse named XXXX was Star!!! Help me. showed me tricks to move around in my condition.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Nurse/Nurse aide, Positive Recognition

Comment: My call button was not plugged in the first night and no one realized. That should have been checked and tested.
MY call button was not working in my room I finded a little bit confusing about my care the ability about follow up was not so good .

My care was very good. However there were lapses in communication that could have minimized my stay. I was admitted with a small pulmonary embolism having already been on xeralto. After diagnosis, discussions with pharmacist, oncologist, I was waiting in emerg to see a hematologist before release. Believing i would see the specialist shortly I was shocked to hear I was being admitted when I asked the next shift nurse what was going on. I was admitted being told the Hematologist would see me in the morning. That morning came and went 2x. When I did see the hematologist, he was great and released me right away. A total of 3 days in hospital. I am happy for the outcome and the people treating me. I wish there was a specialist available to which I would have saved the bed and the expense of a probably unneeded stay. Other feedback - the hospital is very dirty. Having stayed so long, I see the cleaners cleaning yet they seem to just move the dirt into the corners, you can see the build-up of dirt. These are not just stains. I recognize the hospital is old, and being renovated, it can still be clean. I see the efforts and the improvements in the hospital over the last number of years, at core the people are great, the treatment is great. We live between XXXXXX and XXXXXXXX and choose XXXXXX because the treatment is more accurate and better. My feedback is about very small issues. Great job !
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Emergency Dept, Housekeeping/Room, Information/Education

Comment: My cleanliness answers were due to blood on the floor and vomit in the bathroom. My care answers were due to me vomiting excessively and being left in the waiting area with an IV of gravol instead of a bed or anywhere more private.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Housekeeping/Room, Physical Comfort, Infection Prevention & Control

Comment: My condition need ultrasound or MRI because I had some tissue tear I asked for ultrasound they said I didn't one just xray This I believe is a big mistake & caused me distress later my family doctor got me one for my knees

My cot was close to the nurse's station and there was one nurse (XXXX) who spent much of her time in loud personal conversation, and she frequently used obscenity ('fuck this', 'fuck that', 'no fucking way' etc). And when a patient requested help they often had to wait a long time or were ignored. For example, I was on a diuretic and was experiencing a gout flare in my right foot, so found it very difficult to walk, and when I requested a hand held urinal, I had to wait ~ 20 minutes to receive one, despite having received an inter venous dose of Lasix . XXXX told me in a loud scolding voice to be patient and they'd get to me as soon as she could. Some of my fellow patients who were nearby (an elderly lady likely in her 80's needing some water, and an elderly man across the hall seeking help to get up, had to wait ~ 30 minutes, despite being able to hear XXXX in personal conversation with her colleagues (her weight issues, her driving practices, shopping, etc). Not all the nurses were as bad as XXXX, and the physician's care was generally excellent. I was particularly impressed by a young resident (a Dr XXXXXXXX) who had researched my file carefully before speaking with me. Her immediate superior (a physician originally from Poland was also excellent.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient, Positive Recognition

Comment: My dad was brought to ICU on XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and he died on XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.
My daughter had stitches in her eyebrow because of an accident. The visit was very helpful even though it was a medical resident who performed the stitches, she did a great job It went very smoothly.
My daughter was born at XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and my three Grans was born there also. The staff in Emergency Department are nice people - no problem.

My daughter was not allowed in with me and it was sometimes difficult for her to get someone to answer the phone to get updates. I do not use a cell phone and would have liked better ability to communicate with my daughter. A wonderful nurse on day 2 finally brought me a phone to speak to my daughter.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Families/Friends, Information/Education, Nurse/Nurse aide

Comment: My daughter, XX years old, was sent to adult emergency and she had to wait 1 hours, seating on the floor of the hallway! All of her answer on this survey were regarding the adult emergency. She didn't like the experience at all! She asked me not to bring her there again!
My delivery was a great experience! The doctor and nurses were exceptional!

My delivery was unnecessarily rushed by the doctor XXXXXX. She threatened to use forceps and/or preform a c-section after the first ten minutes of pushing my baby out so the second time I hurt myself more than necessary. I won't be going back the hospital based on that experience. Also after stating my fear of the epidural, the anesthesiologist said and I quote: Do you want me to continue (the rundown of possible side effects) or not. It was totally uncalled for.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient

Comment: My doctor at the hospital was XXXXXXXXXXXXXX. I could not have received better care from any other doctor on staff. He's not only a great surgeon, he's a very fine and caring person. Please don't ever promote him to any administrative position. He belongs and I believe he enjoys where he is, with his patients. Obviously, you should give him proper monetary compensation on a regular schedule. This is one individual you cannot afford to lose.
Code: Doctor/Physician, Respect to Patient, Positive Recognition

Comment: My doctor is a very kind and excellent doctor

My doctor on during delivery, XXXXXXX was amazing and made my first child birth experience great. However the room we paid for to stay in, was absolutely freezing and if your paying for a room I expect a more comfortable bed for my husband, we told the nurses 4 times the room was way to cold they said the AC was broke, so it wouldn't shut off in the room they kept us in, they were suppose to see if they could bring in a space heater but I never heard back from Anyone, so my experience was a great one just wish we were placed in a better room.
Code: Billing/Accounting, Doctor/Physician, Families/Friends, Housekeeping/Room, Physical Comfort, Positive Recognition

Comment: My doctor was away, I visited the ER for medicine for eye issue. No pain medina required just antibiotic ointment.
My doctor was excellent.

My doctor was inconsiderate of my past heart problems and thought that me coming to XXXXXXXXXXXX hospital for severe chest pains and breathing issues (despite being rushed in by nurses) was a red flag just because I resided in XXXXXXXX. He thought I was out for pain medications and asked me why I'm not going to XXXXXXXX for help. I tried to explain to him that I had a dietitian appointment at XXXXXXXXXXXX hospital and came straight to the ER after the appointment instead of driving all the way back to XXXXXXXX and waiting up to 10 hours in the ER while I'm having breathing issues and chest pains. He suggested I see my family doctor to get referred to a pain clinic if I want pain meds. I explained to him that I was not there for pain meds, that my history of heart problems and the fact that my family tends to die from cardiac arrests in their XXs (I'm in my XXs), he still ignored everything I was saying. He refused to do any tests other than a ECG which was clear but I didn't believe it was my heart as the pain was on my left side and effecting my breathing. He let me go in tears.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Cardiology, Doctor/Physician, Physical Comfort

Comment: My doctor, XXXXXXXXXXX and nurse, XXXXXXX, were both wonderful!
My emerg visit was awesome, for what it was. The fracture clinic dr. was not as nice or as personable. ER = awesome XX = sucked But, thank you.
Code: Doctor/Physician, Emergency Dept, Respect to Patient

Comment: My emergency department experience was good, however the triage nurse who first saw me was rude and uncaring. She seemed like she hated her job and had absolutely no humanity in dealing with the public and their health concerns. I was in anaphylaxis crying and she was yelling at me. It was awful. I would recommend removing her as a triage nurse as she doesn't reflect the rest of the care I received at XXXXXXXXX.
Code: Admit/Registration, Emergency Dept, Nurse/Nurse aide, Respect to Patient

Comment: My emergency doctor had excellent bedside manners, explained my problem, answered all my questions and made me feel good leaving the emergency department to go home. Thank you!
Code: Doctor/Physician, Emergency Dept, Information/Education, Respect to Patient

Comment: My emergency room doctor was conscientious but so busy, he could hardly have time to explain my diagnosis.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Emergency Dept, Information/Education

Comment: My Emergency visit was fine and with care. But the follow up visit is so uncomfortable. It would be more helpful if the stitches they used on my cut is not need to be removed after it settled because it cause me such pain and uncomfortable and the nurse who removed the stitches just pulled with less care.
Code: Continuity/Transition, Emergency Dept, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort

Comment: My emergency was unusual: my urologist has placed a foley catheter on me while I was on the list for prostate surgery, and the catheter had been blocked by a blood clot in the evening so I went to emergency to get the catheter flushed. But the emergency system was overworked so I waited for 3-4 hours, and then before a doctor or specialist nurse could see me the catheter unblocked by itself, so I left and returned home, and the next morning I could see my urologist who took care of the condition. Three week later I underwent surgery and all is well now. I am very happy about how the surgery went and the assistance I received at XXXXXXXXXXXX.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Emergency Dept, Nurse/Nurse aide

Comment: My entire hospital experience was wonderful from beginning to end. I can't say enough good things about the excellent care I received from labour and delivery nurses XXXXXXX, XXXX and XXX, and from Dr. XXX - 5 weeks post partum and I still look back on them fondly. They made me feel comfortable and confident throughout my labour and delivery. The facilities were modern and clean. I would highly recommend XXXXXXXX to any woman preparing to have a baby.
Code: Doctor/Physician, Emotional Support, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Positive Recognition

Comment: My epidural wore out. The nurses were amazing in trying to find solutions as to why this was occurring. I was told the anesthesiologist was in a case and could not attend to me. We were/expected a visit from the lactation consultant. My husband went to the nurse station to inquire and they called the lactation consultant. We were told she would come in soon. After hours of waiting for her to show up, we left.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Medication/Prescrip, Nurse/Nurse aide

Comment: My experience - on this particular occasion - along with subsequent other serious failures of care and communication - has left me with a very poor opinion of the quality of service at this hospital and reluctant to return. It has also left me with chronic issues owing to failure to provide care in a timely fashion. Other than being ignored and disrespected for most of the day - I also suffered extreme stress as a patient with BP issues, as well as prolonged pain on my right hip from being left lying on my side for nearly 8 hrs, worsening my osteoarthritis I was also suffer from chronic constipation as a results of neglecting a severe case of fecal impaction
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient

Comment: My experience and opinions are based on a one night stay at the hospital. It was a positive experience.

My experience at XXXXXXXXXX's is one I cannot express too highly. From my first visit with Dr XXXXXXX until I was dismissed, I was treated with the utmost care by all the nurses and staff. The care I was given was above and beyond what I was expecting, and I have been boasting to my many friends and family how delighted I am with my experience at XXXXXX's. Many of the people I have spoken to about my hospital stay have expressed the same sentiments as I have. Keep up the great work you are doing.
My experience in emergency was positive experience in semi-private room - food was very unappetizing, bedding was not changed/no towels/soap to wash no offer to change robe.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Dietary/Service, Emergency Dept, Housekeeping/Room, Physical Comfort

Comment: My experience in labour & delivery was absolutely perfect. My nurse, XXXX, was wonderful and made the experience comfortable and stress-free for my husband and me. Comment: Overall it was decent. I needed stitches on my hand (broken glass while washing dishes). I have a few things to say about the overall experience: I went on the hospital's website when the accident happened and couldn't find a thing about where to go to actually get stitches. 'Do I go to Emergency? Some other department? What about late at night like this? I wondered. In fact, the search term 'stitches' returned precisely zero results. One would think there might have been at least SOMETHING on the site about such a common thing as stitches. The thing is, I'm not a frequenter of the hos-pee-tal, and the word Emergency' for me conjures up images of someone falling through a set of sliding doors as they bleed out on the floor. (Too many movies, maybe?) I certainly knew I needed medical attention, but it didn't exactly seem like an emergency with a capital E. Apparently Emergency is a misnomer, since, in the end, that too was the place I ended up getting my stitches REMOVED a few weeks later, and this was hardly an emergency, to say the least. I suppose I just expected the hospital to have something else, more akin to a walk-in clinic, alongside Emergency. But hey, now I know: in the future, just go to Emergency for anything and everything. But I digress. Parking should be free at hospitals. If you show up bleeding/injured/sick, it's not so easy to fumble around with an unintuitive dinosaur-age pay-for-parking machine. Beyond that, I just kept thinking to myself, Y'know, emotionally/physically distraught or grieving families visiting sick loved ones shouldn't have to worry about parking. Why add insult to injury like this? (But this is a separate issue altogether, and so I digress, yet again). Anyway, after I managed to pay for parking with my one usable (but non-dominant) hand, I entered the hospital. The COVID screening person was the first human I came upon. Even they didn't know where I should go to get stitches. 'Ummmm....Probably Emergency,' they told me. So I went to Emergency. When I got there after getting lost due to inadequate and at times unclear signage I was surprised at how fast I was processed. I hardly got time to read a few pages of the book I brought (darn!). But not darn, because I was there to get stitches and get them asap. Right! So I got into the room where the doctor would eventually give me said stitches, but I ended waiting in there for quite some time. (Great! I'll just read my book!) When the doctor finally arrived, he was a pleasant enough fellow, but he did ask me the same question (Have you ever gotten stitches before?) twice within a 5 minute span. And yes, he heard my answer the first time. That was a little concerning. 'Maybe he's just tired,' I thought. 'But wait, do I want someone who's tired wielding a needle and piercing my skin with it?' Anyway, it was fine in the end since he did a good job. He told me the nurse would come and clean my hand up, give me some stuff to bring home, and tell me how to care for the wound. Only she never did because she never came. After an hour of waiting, I decided to lay down on the parchment paper bed (as it was 2 am) and thought I'd try for some sleep. 'If she came in while I was asleep she could wake me,' I thought. 'Maybe I'll go to the reception first just to see if they've forgotten about me. Sure enough, they had. 'Your chart isn't even here anymore, that's strange! they told me. They immediately got a nurse to help me out, so all was well in the end. I was just grateful we have people in society doing this kind of work, so hats off to them! I was also grateful I didn't live somewhere like the United States, where a visit like this one would have run me hundreds (or thousands?) of dollars. Phew! And thirdly I was grateful I didn't get ticketed (since I had only paid for one hour of parking.) I can't recall another time I've been to Emergency, so I was pleasantly surprised at how fast I was processed through the system (or at least wd have been if there wasn't that small mishap.) And I learned something: Emergency is not just for emergencies. I wonder if anyone will even read this.

I wanted to know her name, but she had her name tag hidden and never introduced herself like the other nurses did. Another concern I had was the way I was discharged. I was told by the nurses and doctors that I had the option of leaving at night or the next morning. I chose the morning because I felt I needed more time to recover. Suddenly, a nurse manager walks in the night before my supposed discharge telling me either I leave now or at 2 am because I delivered the baby at 2 am and I can only stay for 48 hours. She told me I cannot stay until the morning as the other nurses and doctors had informed. I don't understand how you can tell someone to leave at 2 am just because they happened to deliver at 2 am. I would have given the hospital a better rating if it weren't for the bad experience I sadly encountered towards the end of my stay.

Comment: Overall, the care at the emergency room was adequate and honestly, the staff at XXXXXXXXX are better than other hospitals in XXXXXXX. My X year old son had the flu and was dehydrated, so we wanted to check his health to ensure it was isolated only to the flu. If I'm being honest, the care was sufficient, it just took far too long and there wasn't enough transparency. Once we saw the doctor after about 5 hours, we were given medicine to give to our son and we were told that we would be checked on in about 30 minutes. We waited for almost 2 hours and no one told us anything, so we had asked the nurse on staff to call the doctor to clear us so we could go and we were told he was elsewhere in the hospital. In total, we were in emergency for 7 hours and we finally left at 1am because my son was begging to go home and was tired, dehydrated, and just wanted to lay in his bed. Unfortunately, our family doctor's clinic was closed, as was our pediatrician's office, so we took our son to the emergency room to confirm that he only had the flu. I understand that sometimes hospitals are understaffed in certain areas, and I also understand that care takes a lot longer in the emergency room, and I recognize that my son wouldn't have been considered an urgent case. However, I think the most frustrating part was the lack of communication. We just kept waiting and no one gave us any updates unless we forced them to. My suggestion is that the communication from staff is worked on in the future. It would really go a long way in terms of patient support. Thank you for sending our family this survey.

Comment: Please note that I was unconscious during admission and can't properly answer you question regarding my admission to your hospital. The door frequently throughout the night would rattle and wake me up. No one asked me if i had a family member or friend that they should call. It felt like the nurses were indifferent. I would have loved to have had a blanket to keep me warm. There was only a hand towel and face cloth. I would have also loved to have had access to an emergency kit which contained shampoo, soap, a toothbrush and toothpaste. Obviously, I never had the opportunity to have a shower and nobody seemed to care. I slept in my clothes all 5 days. There was no dressing gown or robe. When I woke up in a shared room of three, I found I was not wearing any underwear and thought that I meant have been sexually assaulted. That's when I decided I needed to leave and the nurses called security to stop me from leaving. No one bothered to ask me why. My overall impression was one of indifference. This may have been because the nurses did not speak English as their first language and may not have had sufficient English with which to speak to me or it was a cultural difference or due to a difference in training having not been Canadian educated. That's why my rating of your hospital is poor.

As the group of us sat awaiting help in the emergency room waiting area, most of us were clearly distressed already, many of us in pain, and the TV is blasting us with more bad news on top of that, adding to stress levels. By the time I was helped, I had heard the day's murders reported repeatedly - must have heard the story 5 or 6 times. The news was just death, death, death, one theft, and more death (and nearly all the death reported was murder). Regardless of what the news on a given day is, my point is that it is not helping our situations. Please turn the TV off, or if it must be on, put on something light and pleasant: either a light and funny sitcom, or a peaceful nature documentary if it must be a show, or better yet, just display beautiful pictures of nature with nature sounds or 'meditation music' to help keep people calm. I think this would DRAMATICALLY change the environment. Thank you! One of the other patients awaiting treatment was a man who took every opportunity to touch and grope me that he could. I do not think he was in his right mind (seems likely drugs or alcohol were involved) but that is no excuse for me to receive such harassment while I myself am seeking help. I would move to get away, or be called to see a doctor, and he would follow me. I told a doctor about it, and he was wonderful in his response, and initially said that he just assumed that we had come in together, because he was always with me. And I had to say, 'I don't know this guy, and I would like him to leave me alone!' He got security to talk to him and he did stay away from me after that, and I appreciate this very much. The overall detailed roadmap of my care/process was not communicated (partially I will admit is likely because of how quickly I was scheduled for surgery due the level of pain I was experiencing), I felt information was shared just-in time or after the fact such that I did not understand all the steps involved in the preparation, admitting, treatment and care for my condition 6. I received differing directions / incomplete direction by the Physiotherapy staff, I was not clearly aware of what I could/couldn't do after my hip surgery. They also could not provide me the XXXXXXXXXX's patient guide for hip surgery (which I did not receive prior to surgery) as they did not have access to this document. I had to borrow it and take photos from a my roommate who had undergone the surgery a day earlier and was provided the document prior to admission. 7. When an infection was discovered and antibiotics were ordered, I was not provided adequate information or access to a doctor to ask questions. A nurse simply started me on antibiotics and declared 'They found a bug', as a patient and having completed work and studies in microbiology and antibiotic resistance this was very unsettling and created a high level of anxiety. While immediate treatment is critical and provided (Thank you), I felt the on-call doctor should have been present / available to discuss the results of the test and next steps, this did not happen until 24-48 hrs after commencement of therapy. I was also not advised if my doctor was informed of the results and based on his reaction to how I was notified, I assume he was not informed prior to making rounds and assessing my chart. 8. After recovery step of surgery there was confusion on what floor and room I was to be transferred to; which resulted in a short delay in transferring me to my room. This was also unclear prior to surgery requiring my family to back and carry all my personal belonging while I was in surgery; I had hoped that this would have been worked out in the 2-3 hours I was in surgery, if there were complicated reasons I was not made aware. I'd like to again reiterate the satisfaction I had with my medical team. Dr. XXXXXXX in specific was understanding, motivated and committed to get me the best possible care and the necessary tests to make informed decisions and mitigate all possible risks. During the evening, I was seen by the nurse XXXXXXXXXXXXX once when I arrived after surgery, and a second time when I was discharged. Between those times, I was attended to by three other nurses. I understand and appreciate that nurses are overworked, exhausted, and deal with stressful and unpleasant circumstances and people every day. However, there were two situations that occurred during my very short hospital stay that I feel should not have happened; I will try to recount them as briefly as I can. Situation 1: When I needed to go to the bathroom, I pressed the call button. When a nurse (or who I can only assume was a nurse) arrived, she did not introduce herself nor was she wearing a name tag. She did not ask me why I had pressed the button, nor did she help me get out of the bed when it was clear that I was having difficulty doing so on my own. Nurse XXXXXXX had told me earlier that she wanted to be here when I urinated for the first time post- surgery. When I told the nurse without a name tag this, she simply said, 'I am taking you to the bathroom'. When she lead me into the bathroom with my IV stand in her hand, she walked so quickly that I struggled to keep up. After I was seated (unassisted, because she did not make any move to provide assistance), she instructed me to pull the call string if I needed help and/or when I was finished, and then left. When I was finished, I pulled the call string and waited for someone to come. After a few minutes, when no one had arrived, I called to my mother, who was outside the bathroom door, to come in. Still seated on the toilet, I was hit with a wave of nausea and started to heave. There were no pans in the bathroom to heave into, and I could not use the toilet because (1) I was sitting on it, and (2) the urine tray was still attached to the toilet seat. My mother quickly left to find a tray. When she located a group of nurses chatting down the hall, they were not quick to help?their overall demeanor made my mother feel like she was actually causing them a great inconvenience. When my mother finally came back to the bathroom with a pan, a nurse still hadn't arrived, even though the call button in the bathroom was still activated. Thankfully, I had nothing to heave up. My mother helped me back to the bed, at which point I was overcome again with nausea and uncontrollable dry heaving. When the nurse without a name tag finally returned, she looked at the urine sample, consulted with another nurse just inside the hospital room doorway, and then left without coming to check on me. In summary, the fact that a nurse did not come when I pulled the call button/string was concerning, as was the behaviour of the nurses down the hall that my mother encountered. In addition, the utter lack of communication/people skills and sheer disinterest that the nurse without a name tag exhibited was very disconcerting. Situation 2: Later in the evening (between 1:30 AM and 3:30 AM), nursing staff (including another nurse who attended to me during the night) were in the hallway talking very loudly not only about fellow staff members, but also other patients and the details of their conditions. The noise itself was unacceptable, but it was their audacity to gossip about other staff and patients' personal situations that was even more objectionable. I am very grateful for the care given at XXXXXXXXXXXX. Considering what can happen during surgeries and hospital stays, I know that my experience overall went very well (the surgery itself, the fact that there were no complications, infection, etc.). Even so, I felt it was important to share the two above experiences with the belief that improvements can always be made.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Nurse/Nurse aide, Physical Comfort, Respect to Patient, Positive Recognition

Comment: When I came for pre admission interview and blood work I was not made aware that those having surgery would be seen first, so in coming early, on time, I had to wait until those having surgery were admitted - this was not a problem except that I would have come later which would have been better, saving me time and money. Other than that I thought the preadmission doctors, nurses and assistants were most understanding, presented their needs/work to myself very well, asked if there were any problems with understanding, and did so in an extremely personable and interested manner. This public relation attitude was very reassuring that I the patient would be well looked after. I left the pre admission interview in good spirits without trepidation for the upcoming surgery. Now my surgery was not what I would call serious, and I make this comment because if it would have been more serious, I know the hospitals proficiency would have made be feel positive and reassured. The day of admission went very smoothly. I was nervous because needles and the like are unpleasant to me, not so much for pain but just the bodily intrusion. The staff were very considerate and at all point I felt confident in their care. As well I found XXXXXXXXXX's to be extremely clean, nicely renovated for an old hospital, well maintained and friendly. I like that and you should know that not all XXXXXXX hospitals are view as clean, yet if hospitals are not clean then patients must be concerned for their well being, so thank you for having high maintenance standards. After surgery the care was also very good. I understood how my recovery was to proceed, and when irrigation solutions appeared low, I rang for the exchange - the wait time was very minimal, and again that is reassuring for a patient (and I'm not that patient!!!). The night was spent in bed. The next morning when the catheter was to be removed, I was very nervous expecting it to painful. However the nurse told me how she was going do it, got me in the proper frame of mind and did it effortlessly. I thought my care was very good, could not have expected better. I did like the fact that the nurses monitoring station was in the hallway, not at the central desk, and I think that is a great way to locate staff so that the time/distance between patient ringing and nurse/carers is kept to a minimum. When I was able to walk and I had no slippers, I noticed that the floors were very clean, a sign of good hospital management. Again this is care at a higher level than friends have experienced in other XXXXXXX hospital. Thank you and keep up the good work.

Comment: When I first arrived I explained my symptoms to a staff member in a booth by the door. These included cough, chest pain and shortness of breath and that I had been seen there about 3 weeks ago and diagnosed with pneumonia, and that my shortness of breath was now worse. I was directed to sit waiting area A (if I recall correctly) for a triage nurse. One other patient was being served at the triage desk, the other desks were empty. 3 staff members were present at the triage desk. The patient moved on, and I expected to be called. The staff chatted, played what appeared to be games on their phone and played music. I sat there ignored for about 10-15 minutes, there were no other patients waiting. One staff member finally looked at me across the room and asked if i was waiting to be seen!? They called me the desk I described the same symptoms. They were surprised called the person in the booth on the phone and yelled at them as they did not follow protocols. They finally turned their attention to me and commented on how unwell I looked, pale and tired! I was, to say the least, starting to feel very anxious as I was feeling very unwell. They took my information and had difficulty entering my phone number which I had to repeat numerous times. The rest of the visit and care was fine. The doctors and nurses were kind, professional and reassuring. As I was presumed COVID, I greatly appreciated the distancing and safety measures, staff disinfected the chairs in the waiting area 3 times over the course of my 7-8 hours as I waited for tests and results. I was eventually placed in an isolation room for the rest of my stay. The following morning I was seen by 2 other doctors and prescribed blood thinners. I was told I would have a follow up appointment within 3 months at the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX and that they would call me. I never heard from the clinic so after about 4 weeks I called them, they had no record of my visit and could not find my details using the phone numbers I provided (Home and cell), yet the ER doctor called my home # a few days after my visit with test results. I found this to be very disconcerting, that they did not have the right number (even after I repeated numerous times when I arrived at the ER), and that I had to advocate for myself for follow up care. I have additional concerns with respect to that, but that is not related to my ER visit, apart from the telephone number issue. The ER is clearly very tired looking, broken fixtures, walls/ceilings in need of repair and paint, but I very much appreciated the care and assurances I received from the medical team.

Comment: While I understand the importance of this survey, it demonstrates the main problem for me with the ambulatory clinic. You'll notice that my responses are all very positive, but most of the questions didn't apply to my visit. My concerns are with how the clinic is operated, and this was not mentioned. First, everyone that uses the clinic for simple blood-work, to see a dietitian, or for more serious treatment all have to register in the same location. You asked if the hospital changed my appointment to 'a later DATE', which they didn't do, but they did change it to a later TIME. The dietitian, however, was not informed about this so to her I was 1/2 hr late. I got there 1/2 hr before my newly scheduled appointment, but the line up to register was out the door; I left the line to use the kiosk where I was told I can register, but it was not working so I had to go back to the end of the line. There was very little space between 'patients' and still we were asked to move closer together, which was unthinkable given the risk of flu, etc. Lastly, there were many elderly and other people in that registration line that should NEVER have had to stand up waiting. I was appalled that they were expected to do this and there were so few seats available. Thankfully some of those people had someone with them, so they could go outside to sit. I would still be waiting if I required such assistance as I was on my own. I find all the staff and health practitioners to be helpful, friendly and caring - no complaints what so ever, but please reconsider the registration process for appointments. I dread having to go to XXXXXXX's for an appointment. Thank you.

Comment: While I understand the triage process, I wish wait time at Emergency could be shorter (up to 30 minutes). Waiting more than an hour is just too long specially during that COVID-19 pandemic when the number of non-COVID patients was extremely low compared to the usual crowd.

While I was in the waiting room awaiting results for my x-ray there was a man who had breathed some gas and was suffocating. He was begging the people working at the desk who were paramedics I believe for a doctor and they just told him that there weren't any available. This man was literally dying and the paramedics didn't do anything but check his pulse. I was trying to help him breath or figure out what he had breathed but I was told to sit down. Just think they could've helped more.

While I was there, there was a man who seemed to be living in a shelter who was being asked to leave but he could not find his jacket. He was not treated the way that a person who did not live in a shelter would have been treated, in that no one took his concern about his missing jacket seriously. No one offered to check the lost and found, no one asked for a description of the jacket and his number to call him if it was found, no one simply said, I'm sorry we can't find it. Instead one of the people he was asking for help just said 'I don't see a jacket' and the man was urged to leave. Maybe I'm naive and this was some sort of trick the man was playing, though I'm not sure to what end. I know that ER staff are busy, but homeless people are some of the most vulnerable people among us who live lives of constant difficulty and I wish that they could be treated with more compassion. At the time I was there it was actually not very busy at all, and I think if I had misplaced a jacket I would have been treated much better. This man started out polite but became agitated after a while. Treating him with compassion from the start would have prevented the situation from escalating and made everyone's day better. I wonder if there is some sort of training in how to work with the homeless and treat them with compassion that hospital staff could complete. Thank you for hearing my concern.

Perhaps there could be a role of a respiratory therapist in the context of asthma presentation / respiratory compromise which could expedite treatment. Secondly, there was lack of reassessment of vitals / my respiratory condition, while I waited to see a physician for the second time, after having completed an X- ray and received ventolin. This ultimately resulted in a prolonged stay, due to delays in further ventolin treatments. Finally, from a patient care experience perspective, being in visible discomfort / respiratory distress and not having nurses who were close by acknowledge this or come to reassess, felt somewhat frustrating. I recognize that there were likely sicker patients needing immediate attention, which is of upmost importance. However, there was much waiting time between points of contact where care could have been expedited in order for me to be seen more efficiently, and in turn, have other patients seen in a more expedited fashion.

Comment: Although I was very satisfied with the Emergency Department, particularly during COVID19, a scrip error on my 2nd visit necessitated a 3rd visit to the ER, as the prescribing doctor was not on the next day's rotation, so the pharmacist could not validate the scrip. The scrip error did not jeopardize my health, as the prescribed amount was only slightly above the smallest therapeutic dose, however Pregabalin is a capsule and can't be split into the prescribed amount. This also delayed my starting pain treatment until the scrip could be filled the following day. I was also provided a neuro and a family medicine referral as my GP has moved away. After waiting the required 4 business days to be contacted by the neurologist, Dr. XXXXXXXXXXXX's office voicemail recording was very confusing about whether he was seeing new patients or not, considering I was referred from the ER. I left a voicemail, and after not hearing back in the specified 48 hours, I called back and the recording had been updated to state that ONLY IF HE ACCEPTED THE REFERRAL would I be contacted, possibly in 4-5 months due to COVID backlog. When I contacted the family practice number, I was also told they weren't seeing patients in person or taking new patients. So much for continuity of care, as I was told the family practice would have access to my lab work, scan, and clinical assessment. While continuity of care is not an ER accountability, they are a stakeholder. I am very fortunate to have family members in medicine who have advised me on urgency, therapeutic protocols, and necessity for early treatment, so this type of support was very helpful. Apart from the scrip error, I am very satisfied with the care received, but do see room for improvement in the discharge procedures.

Comment: Although my hospital stay was pleasant overall, I felt as though communication about it could have been better. I was told I would be put in a shared room, but instead I was given a private room (which, to be clear, was a nice surprise!). I was unclear about how meals worked or when to expect them. And on the morning that I left, I was told vaguely that 'we'll just need to finish up with some paperwork and you'll be free to go,' but I actually had no idea when those papers would be done, and I ended up confused as to when I should tell my family to pick me up.  Also, though I'm sure they were doing their best, the nurses seemed a bit overworked and frazzled -- in particular, I had to remind the night nurse to take out my catheter, which resulted in me having an uncomfortable catheter in my body for longer than was really necessary. I also would have preferred to know beforehand that nurses would be visiting me throughout the night, so that I wouldn't be expecting a full night's sleep.  The nurses also seemed somewhat confused about my gender, with several of them misgendering me as female (I am a trans man). They took well to being corrected, but I would have been more comfortable if they had avoided gendering me or followed my surgeon's lead (as he did gender me correctly and consistently).  Overall, I felt that my care was good but somewhat disorganized.

Background: On XXXXXX I had an ischemic stroke. My motor skills were affected, my perception was altered so I could not hold a fork, close a zipper or walk without falling. I soon learned in the ambulance, my ability to speak was gone - only gibberish came out of my mouth - I could not speak a coherent sentence or identify graphic pictures or printed words that were flashed in my face by the team of stroke doctors. Thanks to the swift intervention by a phenomenal team of dedicated stroke specialists and the unbelievable care I received at XXXXXXXXXXXX, there were no motor or cognitive deficits, my speech came back within a few hours and now I am home, shell shocked but so grateful to be alive and intact. I have only praise and gratitude for everyone connected with XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. The care I received was exceptional. What follows are some of the things that I experienced as a patient during my stay and when I went home that could do with some improvement. Emergency Room and Hospital Care: The stroke team of doctors addressed me in a normal tone of voice in the emergency room. The young female nurses however raised their voices to an uncomfortably loud level, speaking at me rather than to me as I lay on the gurney. I am XX but it should not be assumed the elderly are deaf or incapable of understanding unless voices are twice normal level. Being nearly shouted at with questions is alarming. This is not a complaint, just something that could be made better because overall my care in the emergency room was exceptional. MRI: By the time I had my MRI on XXXXXX, I had been 18 hours without food or water. Being wheeled through long corridors, over bumps, in and out of elevators to reach the MRI room took some time and the experience of looking up at the moving ceiling on an empty stomach and being generally very stressed after the stroke, resulted in nausea and vertigo. The attendants who wheeled me around that day were engaged ina very loud personal conversation with each other and laughing, behaving as if they were transporting a sack of potatoes. It would be better if the attendants who push patients on gurneys through the hospital recognize there is a person in discomfort on the gurney and provide a quiet respectful ride. This situation happened only once - most attendants were very careful. The Discharge: When I was discharged from XXXXXXXXXXXX I was given a 242 page binder containing information with hundreds of web sites with more information. This is information overload that I found overwhelming to deal with when I got home. The sheer quantity of material and much of what I was reading was frightening and not conducive to recovery in the days following a stroke. I realize patients are diverse in terms of health education. I do appreciate the informative contents of the binder but I would really have preferred to have a doctor or nurse talk to me before I left the hospital explaining what I might expect from my body as I recovered. As I am learning, the stroke recovery trajectory is not linear with each day better than the last but more a case of one step forward, two steps back. A resident did speak to me before I was discharged but was vague with respect to my questions about the recovery process and what I might experience. It is now 6 weeks later and I still don't know why I am having the symptoms I am dealing with and whether they are related to my stroke or, being weaned abruptly from a beta blocker after 16 years, or the result of my body adjusting to a new medication - 80mg of Lipitor, or a new cardiac problem. Question 38 on the Questionnaire: Question 38 on the questionnaire asks whether I had enough information about what to do if I was worried about my condition after I left the hospital. My answer was "not at all". This has been a problem for me. I have seen my doctor who glanced at the discharge summary but gave me little information or reassurance about my symptoms. The disrge binder listed the name and contact information of each member of the XXXXXXXXXXXX stroke team but I was not able to reach them, only their voicemail. The Clinical Nurse Specialist however was accessible and she did provide help on the phone. Patient needs to know whom to contact after discharge: In my opinion it is very important that a patient knows whom to contact if a situation arises after discharge. Who is in charge? The stroke team doctors left the decision of whether to resume taking the beta-blocker to my family doctor who said little to me about the matter. In the weeks after my stroke, a clear understanding of whom to contact about my symptoms would have been appreciated. As it was I connected mostly with voicemails and unfortunately left to fend for myself. Stroke Survivor Liaison Group: In addition to having a clear idea of what to expect during recovery and whom to contact once discharged, a stroke survivor liaison might also have been effective in calming my anxieties after being discharged. The contact provided in my binder (XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) has yet to return my call after 3 messages. There are breast cancer survivor support groups. A stroke survivors support group should be beneficial. I have watched the online videos provided by links are in the binder, but human support would be infinitely better. I found the sounds interesting and the computer generated voice announcing the length of each scan to be reassuring as it is similar to the voice that announces the next station on the TTC. I only wish the clinical staff on the floor had the compassion and empathy necessary to ensure proper patient care and satisfaction.

From Attachment -  My surgical procedure was well managed and successful.  Communication was good, the team professional and competent.  A problem arose after an angiogram the day before when I wasn't permitted to rise to urinate.  There was a fear the incision (in my groin) might bleed.  The nurse had instructions to keep me flat on my back, but I felt I was going into urinary retention (I have BPH and had previous episodes of retention) and tried to explain I needed to pee.  She was insistent and I wanted to co-operate and probably wasn't assertive enough.  When I was allowed to rise I was in retention.  What followed was 10 efforts to catheterize me through my enlarged prostate - three nurse tried and then the nurse practitioner.  Again, I probably should have been more assertive.  When all were unsuccessful the urology resident was called and was successful.  This experience was intensely painful - bleeding, bladder spasm, distension.  Since leaving the hospital I have had several trial voids with negative results and more trouble with re-catherization and controlling my bleeding, including a two day hospital stay.  My urologist performed a cystoscopy and found evidence of scar tissue that may be complicating a problem that we had earlier been successful treating with medication.  I will require TURP surgery.  Unfortunately, I have been prescribed a anti platelet drug following my surgery at St. Mike's (brain aneurysm) and so the surgery cannot be performed until I can go off the medication.  I am currently living with an indwelling catheter.  My quality of life has been severely affected.  While I appreciate catherization is usually a fairly uncomplicated procedure and that medicine is not a precise science, I think it would be useful to develop a post-surgical protocol that takes pre-existing conditions into consideration more fully.  Things would likely have gone better if I had been allowed to pee, and if the urology resident had been called after two or three rather than ten unsuccessful attempts at catherization.  I am usually a reasonably assertive person and have been puzzled by my own behaviour that day.  I assume it must be related to the feelings of vulnerability and dependence induced by being in a position where you are basically trusting other people with your life.  I offer these comments not in a spirit of bitterness but with the intention of helping the hospital avoid similar misadventures.
Code: Access/Coord of Care, Doctor/Physician, Information/Education, Physical Comfort, Radiology, Respect to Patient

My husband and I were literally shivering during our entire hospital stay. I did everything in my power to get released early (in just over 24 hours with a c section) because we didn't want to recover in those conditions any longer...I would have wanted to stay longer considering how I felt in my recovery process but I couldn't withstand freezing temperatures any longer. These conditions are absolutely unacceptable and just downright horrendous. Imagine being in the most pain you've ever felt caring for a newborn child in absolute freezing temperature to the point your nose feels frozen and you're shivering ... it was just so awful I couldn't believe it ... this to me should be a basic provision. More over, nursing staff seemed a lot younger than my last stay and less compassionate and less forth coming of advice or any additional help. I asked for a new gown after bleeding through and was left naked under the sheets. I was rarely cleaned or checked up on. Several times my pain meds were not given to me on time and I had to get my husband to go ask for my next dose while full on pain was kicking in. Considering nursing staff were mainly leaving us be I expected at least my pain meds to be brought on time. Some other small stuff that just amplified the terrible experience, was the bathroom was not cleaned when we took over the room as a dirty bed pan was left over the toilet, your hospital didn't have disposal padded underwear simply just massive pads I guess to just stick there, every time I asked for a gown over even a pad, I was always asked if I brought my own stuff first before they gave me anything, newborn bath care was non existent ... they didn't do it or show me how to do it and simply said that newborns don't need a bath, on more than a few occasions my husband was told to stand back or leave the room while nurses congregated around me which I'm not sure why and it definitely made him feel not so great, I asked for gas x and stool softener and was told they didn't have any which was surprising. Based on this experience, there is no way I can possibly recommend people coming to your hospital to have their baby under these conditions.
